title: Chrome DevTools MCP = X-ray vision for frontend
description: Chrome DevTools MCP is insane for frontend dev. It gives your agent X-ray vision into the browser while it tests what youre building - it reads console logs, runtime errors, stack traces, hydration issues, failed API calls, bad auth headers, CORS errors, missing assets. It does DOM inspection so it sees what actually rendered, not just what your React or Vue tried to render. It can even check session cookies, auth state, local and session storage. Pair it with the Playwright MCP and your agent can drive the browser AND inspect every code-relevant error as it navigates, a real testing and validation loop. I think thats the ultimate setup for agent frontend development. Comment Chrome and Ill send you the links to both tools.
transcript: Guys, the Chrome Dev Tools MCP is insane for front-end development. It basically gives your agent x-ray vision into your browser while you're testing the front end that you're developing. So, your agent can see a ton of different metadata, logs, errors about that front end you're developing. It has a get console logs tool, so you can actually see run-time errors, stack traces, hydration issues, and a bunch of other stuff. It can see failed API calls, it can see incorrect off headers, it can see cores errors. It can see if there are missing assets in your front end, if there are wrong payloads, just a ton of different metadata from those logs. It can also do something called DOM inspection, which means it can actually see what the browser rendered, not just what your like React or Vue code was trying to render. It can also inspect things like session cookies if that's relevant to the front end you're making, things like off state, persistence issues, local storage, session storage, so many things. Pairing something like this with something like the Playwright CLI or Playwright MCP unlocks an extra superpower, so now your agent can use the browser, but it can also use the Chrome DevTools MCP to really inspect all the code relevant errors in the browser as it's navigating. Creating a testing and validation loop using both the Playwright MCP and the Chrome DevTools MCP, I think may be the ultimate way to do agentic front-end software development. If you want the links to both of those tools, just comment Chrome below and I will send it over to you via DM.
